lines.say: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons. Electrons surround it, about 1 in 1836 of a proton's mass.
lines.write: p⁺, n⁰ in nucleus · e⁻ outside

lines.say: Atomic number Z is the number of protons. It defines the element.
Mass number A is protons plus neutrons.
Isotopes have the same Z, but different numbers of neutrons. Same chemistry.
Chlorine is 75.78 percent chlorine 35, and 24.22 percent chlorine 37.

draw.alt: Bar split 75.78 percent Cl-35 and 24.22 percent Cl-37

lines.say: Weighted average: 26.500 plus 8.953. A r is 35.45.
Light is a wave. Speed equals wavelength times frequency.
Light is also photons. Each carries energy h nu, or h c over lambda.
Excited gases give off only certain wavelengths. That's a line spectrum.

draw.alt: Dark band with a few bright coloured lines

lines.say: Sharp lines mean the electron's energy is quantised. Only fixed levels allowed.
Bohr gave hydrogen's electron fixed energy levels, labelled n.
Energies are negative because the electron is bound. Zero means it's removed.
Drop from n 3 to n 2. The atom gives out a photon.

draw.alt: Energy levels with electron dropping from n=3 to n=2 and emitting a photon

lines.say: Delta E is 2.18 times 10 to the minus 18, times a quarter minus a ninth.
Lambda equals h c over delta E. That's 656 nanometres, a red line.
Bohr works for hydrogen, but fails for atoms with two or more electrons.
Heisenberg: we can't know an electron's position and momentum exactly.
De Broglie: any moving particle has a wavelength.
Schrödinger described the electron with a wavefunction, psi.
Psi squared gives the probability of finding the electron. An orbital is a region, not a path.
n is the shell: size and energy. It goes 1, 2, 3 and so on.
l is the shape, from 0 to n minus 1. s, p, d, f.
lines.write: l = 0 … n − 1 → s p d f

lines.say: m l is the orientation, from minus l to plus l. So 2 l plus 1 orbitals.
m s is the spin: plus a half or minus a half.
For n equals 3: one s, three p, five d. Nine orbitals, up to 18 electrons.
s orbitals are spheres. p orbitals have two lobes, with a nodal plane.

draw.alt: Spherical s orbital and two-lobed p orbital with nodal plane

lines.say: Most d orbitals have four lobes.
An orbital has l angular nodes and n minus l minus 1 radial nodes.
A 3 p orbital has one angular node and one radial node.
Report wavelength as positive. Just use the size of delta E.
Convert nanometres to metres before using E equals h c over lambda.
There's no 1 p or 2 d. l must be less than n.
An orbital is a probability cloud, not an orbit.
